title: Behavioral & HR for Python Freshers — Revision

sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Behavioral rounds account for 30-50% of a fresher interview. Technical skill gets you in the door; communication and self-awareness close the offer. Every answer needs to be structured, specific, and honest.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
**Four-part self-introduction formula:**

1. **Education** — degree, institution, year (10 seconds)
2. **Project** — one sentence: what problem, what tech, what you built (20 seconds)
3. **Skill highlight** — the Python/backend skill most relevant to this role (10 seconds)
4. **Why this company** — one specific reason (10 seconds)

Total: under 60 seconds. Practice until it's fluent, not recited.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **Self-introduction** — problem→solution→result structure. Not a feature list of your project.
- **'Why Python?'** — genuine answer: readable syntax, rich ecosystem for backend (Django, FastAPI), strong community. Never: 'it's easy'.
- **Strength** — pick one that's relevant (e.g., 'I break problems into small pieces before coding'). Give one example.
- **Weakness** — real but not disqualifying. Show you're working on it. 'I sometimes over-engineer solutions — I've learned to ask myself if a simpler approach exists first.'
- **Team conflict** — STAR structure. Disagreement → what you did → positive outcome.
- **Failure** — own it fully. What went wrong, what you learned, what you'd do differently.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **'Tell me about yourself'** — the opener. Have it memorised but not robotic.
- **'Why should we hire you?'** — connect your specific skills to what the role needs.
- **'Where do you see yourself in 3 years?'** — realistic: 'contributing to production features, deepening my Python backend expertise, taking on more ownership.'
- **'Do you have any questions for us?'** — always yes. 'What does onboarding look like for new joiners?' / 'What tech stack will I work with?'

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"Keep answers specific — name the technology, name the outcome, name what you learned. Generic answers ('I'm a fast learner', 'I work well in teams') are invisible. Specific answers ('I debugged a 3-day recursion issue by adding print statements at each call level and found the missing base case') are memorable."*
